known_differences_from_fetch_script: Rape is not mappable: the pull has no sex-offense category (43 distinct Crime_Description values in raw_cache_profile.json, none Rape/Sodomy/Sexual Assault With An Object/Fondling), and the layer's type domain (doc_00.json 'types', 45 entries) has none either, so the publisher withholds sex offenses without stating it. Official rape totals (41-56 a year 2023-2025, official_totals.csv) have no feed counterpart.

Unit: one row per (Case_Number, Crime_Description); Case_Number repeats across categories (20223 rows, 17359 distinct Case_Number, 20223 distinct Case_Number|Crime_Description, query on raw_cache). Several offenses of the same category in one case (e.g. several aggravated-assault victims or several larcenies) collapse to one row, and an incident with several of the seven offenses counts once in each; SRS summary totals (2018-2020 sources in official_totals.csv) apply the hierarchy rule and count one offense per incident.
Date is the report date (Reported_DateTime), not the occurrence date, which is not published; year boundaries can shift offenses between years relative to the official totals.

Coverage: the archived pull for 2018-2025 returns only 2023-01-01 05:52 UTC through 2025-12-31 22:51 UTC (6478/6724/7017 rows for 2023/2024/2025, make_timestamp(Reported_DateTime*1000) grouped by year); 2018-2022 have no rows, although doc_00.json timeInfo.timeExtent starts 1641021300000 (2022-01-01), so the layer appears to be a rolling window and a later live pull may lose early years.

Categories straddling definitions: none of the mapped labels straddle two offenses; they are the NIBRS offense names (09A, 120, 13A, 220, 23A-23H, 240). Manslaughter by negligence (3 rows), Justifiable Homicide (1), Simple Assault (1432), Intimidation (428) and Arson (43) are left unmapped per the FBI definitions.

notes: Source: the Duluth PD Mapped_Crimes ArcGIS layer (registry_row.json), a NIBRS-category offense feed: Crime_Description carries NIBRS offense names (raw_cache_profile.json distinct values; doc_00.json typeIdField 'Crime_Description'). Mapping: Murder/Nonnegligent Manslaughter -> murder (09A); Robbery -> robbery (120); Aggravated Assault -> aggravated_assault (13A); Burglary/Breaking & Entering -> burglary (220); Pocket-Picking, Purse-Snatching, Shoplifting, Larceny from Building, Larceny from Coin Operated Machine or Device, Larceny from Motor Vehicle, Larceny of Motor Vehicle Parts or Accessories, Larceny All Other -> larceny (23A-23H); Motor Vehicle Theft -> motor_vehicle_theft (240). Every mapped label is present in the pull (counts in raw_cache_profile.json). Rape stays unmapped: no sex-offense category exists in the pull or in the layer domain. Excluded: Manslaughter by negligence (09B), Justifiable Homicide (09C), Simple Assault (13B), Intimidation (13C). Count unit is offense: Case_Number|Crime_Description is unique on every row (20223 = 20223 distinct, query), so id_fields = [Case_Number, Crime_Description] and dedupe_on_id is a no-op kept as a guard; a case with several categories keeps one row per category, and the rules assign each row by its own Crime_Description. Date: Reported_DateTime (alias 'Reported Date & Time', esriFieldTypeDate, doc_00.json fields) parsed as epoch_ms; it is the report date, because no occurrence date is published. doc_00.json dateFieldsTimeReference gives UTC; the runner's year is taken from the epoch value. Coordinates: the published Latitude/Longitude fields, identical to the feature geometry (max |Latitude-__arcgis_latitude| = 5.0e-9, same for longitude, query); no zero points. The publisher does not state rounding or offsetting, but points appear block-level: 20223 rows sit on 5945 distinct points against 2939 distinct BlockAddress values ('NNNN BLK street'), e.g. 877 rows at '1200 BLK E Superior St' on 3 points (query). Scope: Duluth city only (scope_candidates.csv, registry jurisdiction_ids); 13 rows carry City Hermantown/Proctor/Rice Lake/Hibbing and 5 are null (raw_cache_profile.json), left to the footprint join. Pull counts vs official totals for 2023/2024/2025 (feed rows by Crime_Description and UTC year, before location/footprint filters, vs official_totals.csv): murder 2/5/5 vs 1/7/4; robbery 31/36/33 vs 31/33/34; aggravated assault 134/113/107 vs 141/112/120; burglary 288/252/230 vs 281/242/222; larceny 2221/2395/2489 vs 2086/2249/2357; motor vehicle theft 170/115/114 vs 157/109/99. The where clause is the registry probe_where, which is the filter the archive was pulled with (packet.json case_text); page_size 2000 is the layer maxRecordCount (doc_00.json). No redactions or exclusions are stated (registry redactions empty; layer description empty).
